metadata.name: dsh-pajama-whale

paragraphs.text: A draggable pet in a blue-whale onesie for DeepSeek Harness: sticks to the window edges, squashes fl
at, blinks, sleeps, and reports agent status in a thought cloud.
# 🐋 dsh-pajama-whale
**Meet the typical DeepSeek Harness developer.**

A toy-sized colleague in a blue-whale onesie who lives in your DSH window —
and tells you what the a
gent is doing while you wait.
English · 中文

He is a desk toy first and a status indicator second. Push him around the
window, fling him at a wal

l — he squashes flat against it and stays pinned
there until you drag him away. Nothing breaks: no g

ravity, no damage, no
opinions about your code. Leave him alone and he dozes off.

Play with him while a long turn runs. He pulls out a laptop when tools start,
pops a thought cloud w

hen you are needed, and speaks up when the context is
running out, when a turn failed, or when you h

ave been at it for fifty minutes
straight.

No configuration. No network calls of its own. The whole thing is one overlay
slot.
## Install
**Web** (verified on DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`):

tagged GitHub source? Us

e
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:lubenkov/dsh-pajama-whale#v0.3.6`
(requires `git`).

**Desktop, from a terminal.** The npm `dsh` CLI refuses the reserved `desktop`
profile. Install the

command from the app menu **Manage dsh Command…**, quit
the app, then run:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Reopen the app afterwards.

**Desktop, in the app.** Open the **Plugins** page and install
`dsh-pajama-whale` there. Keep the ap
p running and follow its restart prompt.
To remove him:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

No build step at install time: the artwork ships inlined in `client.js`, so
`dsh plugin add` is all

it takes — no postinstall hook, no runtime downloads.
It is a pure UI bundle (no dependencies, no ho

st services beyond the ones it
reads through).

**Declared for DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`** in `engines.dsh`. DSH enforces it
at installation and p

rofile startup; outside the range it refuses the bundle
until an exact-version exemption is granted.

When listed, the market index
carries its own copy of the range, so both must be kept in sync. See

COMPATIBILITY.md for the API surface, the exemption
command, and what degrades gracefully.
## Play with him
| You | He |
| Drag | Follows the pointer. Release slowly and he stays put; release fast (>120 px/s) and he flies

. No gravity, no bouncing. |
| Drag into a wall | Sticks to it, flat: four directions × 8 frames, an
d the frame is picked by how far you overshoot (up to 110 px) or, after a throw, by impact speed. |
| Click | Shows the current context pressure (or the session title when it is unknown) in the cloud

for 5 s. |
| Hover the cloud | Same context reading, while the cursor is there. |
| Click the cloud
| Opens the session he is watching. |
## He follows the agent
| What the session does | What he does |

| A tool has run in this turn | Switches to the `working` pose — laptop out, 12 frames |
| Turn runn

ing, no tool activity | `thinking`, 20 frames |
| Turn finishes | One `joy` burst |
| Waiting for yo

ur approval or an answer | Cloud shows `?` |
| Last turn failed | Cloud shows `! error` for 6 s |
|
Context pressure reaches 80 % | One `surprised`; cloud shows `context N%` while it stays ≥80 %, and

`surprised` re-arms below 75 % |
| 50 min of continuous work | Cloud suggests `take a break?` for 9

s (repeats every 45 min; a pause under 3 min still counts as continuous) |
| A minute of quiet | Fal
ls asleep on a looping 16-frame `sleepy`; a yawn (13 frames) when you wake him with the cursor — a n
ew turn wakes him silently |

While idle he only blinks (75 %) or wags his tail (25 %), every 1.9–4.5 s, plus
a rare `hmm…` though

t. That is 129 frames across 12 sprite sheets. While you
drag him or while he is stuck to a wall, po

ses and one-shot emotions pause: the
squash frame wins.
### One cloud, strict priority

`hover` / `click` context → `?` waiting → `! error` → `take a break?` →
`context N%` at ≥80 % → idle

`hmm…` (3.6 s, every 70–160 s). Hovering or
clicking always wins, so the pet never hides the contex

ry 70–160 s). Hovering or
clicking always wins, so the pet never hides the context reading from you.
## Cheap and quiet

- **Nothing to build, nothing to fetch.** All 12 sheets (2.3 MB of WebP,
129 frames) are inlined as

data URIs into a single 3.1 MB `client.js`. The
plugin makes no outbound requests of its own.
- **Ch

eap when idle.** The `requestAnimationFrame` loop stops as soon as the
pet is idle and no pose is pl

aying. Sprite frames advance at each animation's
own rate — 8 fps for `sleepy`, 10 for `yawn`, 12 fo

r `thinking` and `working`,
14 for tail, joy and `surprised`, 16 for `blink`. Breathing is a ~3.4 s

CSS
animation every 25–40 s. While the tab is hidden the browser suspends
`requestAnimationFrame` an

d breathing is stopped explicitly; the status
ticker and idle-thought timer are throttled by the bro

wser but not cancelled.
Breathing and random emotions are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`
(p

ose animations still play).
- **Never in your way.** He mounts only into `shell.overlay`, and the ov

erlay
is `pointer-events: none` outside his body and cloud.
- **Remembers his place.** Position, wal

l and squash depth live in
`localStorage` and are clamped when the window resizes.
## Language and privacy

English and Chinese strings follow Settings → Language through `ctx.locale`
(anything else falls bac

k to English). The plugin reads only session status,
context pressure, session title and recent tool

activity to choose a pose. It
sends nothing anywhere, has no telemetry, and stores only the pet's p

osition,
wall side, squash depth and stuck flag in `localStorage` on your machine.
## If he does not show up

1. Confirm the profile you installed into is the one you boot.
2. Check the DSH version against the

declared range. Outside it, installation
or profile startup refuses the bundle; grant an exact-versi

on exemption only
after accepting the risk (see COMPATIBILITY.md).
